surfaces.part: TV and screen on the stand top

answer.evidence: The main body is a drawer cabinet, not an open frame, so the kind does not match well. Its top is a tan band that runs from about row 13 to row 20 and is visible left and right of the TV base. It ends in a light front-edge line at row 21 (#ddbf91), followed by a darker shadow row at 22. Below that is a drawer front of about 10 rows (22-31). The TV and the plant sit on the top as decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden TV stand with a monitor and a small plant. The measured facts are decent: 12 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the stall and 20 for the well, 15% near-flat coverage (similar to the stall's 13%), and 44% near-neutral dark edges (the same as the bench). By eye, the wood body shows only about 3 steps (a light top, a mid body and a dark drawer or base), where Beodeul wood has 5-6 with grain and per-plank highlights. The TV screen is mostly a flat dark blue block with a single highlight. The outline leans dark but is only partly tinted, so it reads as mixed rather than a clear dark-material tone. Texture is modest, with a few grain marks on the cabinet and some leaf variation on the plant. Overall it is acceptable and clean but thinner and flatter than the stall and well references, and shallower in shading than a careful Beodeul piece.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden TV stand with a monitor and a small plant. Dark edge pixels are 44% neutral, the same as the bench and below the lamp at 100%, so the outline is mixed. Visually, the wood cabinet shows about 3-4 steps with a plank top, two drawers and a few grain dots. The monitor is a fairly flat dark blue screen with a light bezel, and the plant has only a couple of greens. This is thinner than the stall and well, which carry 5-6 steps with per-element highlights and grain. The piece is clean and acceptable but a little shallower than the richest references. Because the outline is partly neutral and the shading is shallow on the screen and plant, it is not clearly at the Beodeul bar.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small cabinet with a monitor and a potted plant. It has 12 visible tones per tile, which is above the hedge (9) but below the stall (17) and well (20). Its 21 total colours are about half the 38-40 of the comparable props. Near-flat coverage is 15%, in line with the stall's 13%, but the picture shows the TV screen, the dark bezel and the cabinet front as fairly flat slabs. The wood ramp has roughly 3-4 steps against about 6 on the references, with little grain or per-plank highlight. Dark edge pixels are 44% near-neutral, so the outline is mixed: part tinted, part neutral black, giving some of the sticker look. The Beodeul pieces instead use tinted dark-material outlines selectively and shade each surface in more steps. The piece is clean and readable but shallower in shading and texture than the references, so with doubt it fails.
